featured_reviews.name: Farhan Birjandi
featured_reviews.review_text:
I’ve stopped by Coffee Capital a few times recently, and every drink I’ve tried has been seriously good.
First up was the Mocha Chip — rich, chocolatey, and with just the right coffee kick.

The next day, I went for the Espresso Hot Chocolate. Super smooth, cozy, and perfectly balanced — not too sweet, with that deep espresso flavor coming through. Definitely a go-to for cooler days.

I also had a sip of the Coconut Espresso (wasn’t mine, but I had to try it), and it was surprisingly great. The coconut added a subtle sweetness that worked so well with the espresso — different, but in the best way.

The staff is another highlight. Muskaan was a delight on my first visit — super friendly and made the experience feel welcoming from the start. The next day, Alfiya was just as pleasant. She’s got a great vibe and really knows how to make you feel comfortable while you wait for your drink. Great service all around.

If you’re nearby, definitely check this place out. Great drinks, great vibes, and even better service.

Their maggie and peri peri fries are equally delicious and are my go-to comfort food. What I truly appreciate is the consistency in taste and quality, which keeps me coming back again and again.

featured_reviews.name: Pooja Shukla
featured_reviews.review_text:
Lovely place to visit. No alcohol served.
The ambiance is more of a street cafe from London/Paris! I like it.

Different types of seating available - sofa type, chairs, table to 2, table for 3 and more.

We've been there multiple times. I'll list the dishes which I remember 🤪

1. Paneer shashlyk Sizzler in Makhani Sauce - This is served with panner in satay sticks, butter rice and veggies, fries, wedges, corn n cheese stuffed capsicum. As Makhani is supposed to be a sweet thing a bit, I loved this one. It's sweet n spicy. Should try this for veg!

2. Paneer sizzler - Though the name is a bit similar to the previous one but this is completely different. This is served with butter rice and gravy with paneer served on top of the rice. The gravy is covered with melted cheese, and it's delicious. Served with veggies and fries.

3. Teekha Paneer Burger - Burgers are served in Tiffin boxes served with fries. The bun was a little dry, but the patty and sauces, veggies made it tasty.

4. Farmhouse Pizza - Chunky pieces of paneer, olives, mushrooms, bell peppers, corn, and cheeeseee!!! The crust was soft and freshly made. One thing I wish that the  paneer in the pizza should have been marinated with some spices as it tasted blant.

5. Cheese Garlic Bread - This is a must try. Melted gooey cheese with super soft bread🤌

6. Virgin Mojito - A classic beverage you can't go wrong with. Must try!

Overall, it is a good place to visit and hang out with your friends for some chitchat.

featured_reviews.name: ワルドヨエヂ
featured_reviews.review_text:
Last weekend, I had dinner with friends at Cafe Delhi Heights, and it was a fantastic experience. Since I’ve been here before, I knew what to expect—good food and a lively atmosphere—but this visit confirmed why it’s one of my favorite places for a weekend hangout.

The highlight of our meal was the steak made from Merbau beef, which was tender, juicy, and full of flavor. If you love a good steak, this is definitely a must-try. We also ordered the salmon, which was cooked perfectly—crispy on the outside and moist on the inside. The menu offers a variety of other interesting dishes, making it a great spot even for those who aren’t looking for Indian cuisine.

The ambiance here is fun and energetic, perfect for a Saturday night out. The only downside was that the music was a bit too loud, making it hard to have a relaxed conversation. Because of this, it’s not the best place if you want to stay for a long, cozy meal.

Overall, Cafe Delhi Heights is highly recommended, especially for those seeking non-Indian options in a vibrant setting.
